scope: Focused text-only editorial review of immutable source segments 1041–1120 (80 segments). All 338 source word occurrences are preserved in exact spelling and order: 323 eligible and 15 excluded sound/action-description occurrences. Includes 323 contextual explanations and 323 four-option choice overrides covering every eligible occurrence; 4 segments are wholly non-educational. Personal names remain eligible even inside pure action brackets; everyone-laughs descriptions remain non-educational. A in 1041 is retained as an attested Turkish interjection, consistent with the source gloss, not expanded into an invented word; the publisher-hosted Turkish pronunciation dictionary supports its interjection status, not audiovisual certainty about this utterance. Ha, Heh, Oha, Çüş, be, lan, ya and lexical hesitation Şey are retained. No nonlexical incomplete hesitation syllable, incomplete word, or unresolved spelling/name error requiring a hold was identified. Sentence truncation after the complete kaçırıp and ben does not exclude those words. Context separates search arıyorum from telephone calling, figurative beynim yandı, father self-reference, permission izni from a third party's approval, literal and filler şey, future purchase almayacağım from taking money, piyango çıkmış, seasonal Kışın/Yazın, and the nominalized ability yaşayabilmekmiş. The bıdık reference supports its physical lexical sense; its affectionate function is a textual contextual inference. Sıçtırtma is preserved as a vulgar causative prohibition rather than silently standardized; the Turkish university reference supports stacked causative morphology generally, not the film's exact idiomatic force. Characters' talk about illness, coercion, suicide, religion and insults is explained as dialogue, without medical diagnosis or endorsement. References are linguistic metadata only. No audiovisual verification, native-speaker certification, device acceptance, or full-film editorial acceptance is claimed.
